items.section: 4.7 DNA replication and repair — the self copying itself, and the protection of the copying
items.sentence: Fidelity is bi-inversioning protection of copying — one same protection cell cycle's checkpoints have (a self recursioning to a new form), here with base.
items.text: In a bacterium the inherited strand carries methyl marks at its GATC sites and the strand newly made carries none until the methylase reaches it, a window the field measures at about one to two minutes behind the fork, and in that window mismatch repair is directed to the strand without marks; cells with a nucleus carry no such mark, and there the strand newly made is known by its nicks and by ribonucleotides misincorporated in it. After the window the two strands are not told apart. An explaining beside it: the two strands of a pair are the one inherited, the same thing it was before the fork, prior-existing with the cell, and the one forming at the fork, now-existing with the cell; the cell's own repair tells the two apart for a measured while and goes to the forming strand only, and at the window's end the forming strand is inherited. Now-existing with the cell has a length at a strand that the field has measured, and the one binary is with marks or without, is or is not.

items.section: 4.7 DNA replication and repair — the self copying itself, and the protection of the copying
items.sentence: Two strands of double helix separate, and each serves as template for a new complementary strand, each new molecule with one original strand and one fresh — a self recursioning to two, each bringing form forward.
items.text: An explaining, with the three observings held at this section, density labelling, the bean's chromatids with their exchanges and the random or nonrandom parting of chromatids: the co-sequencing of an inherited strand with a forming strand is all or none at the nucleotide and at the fork, and at no larger count. At a fork each pair has one strand from before and one forming, never both of either and never a strand part one and part the other. Each nucleotide of a strand joined it at one fork and at no other. A strand over a lifetime is not wholly of one fork, repair replacing pieces of it; a chromatid after a sister exchange is inherited along one part of its length and forming along the other; a cell's inherited strands go to one daughter or part at random; at each of these larger counts the field's own observing is the binary holding one scale down, at the nucleotide.
